text:
maria: quick idea - add a dedicated "binding.namespace" field to rollout metadata so clients can deterministically decide visibility without parsing labels :thinking:

alex: curious - aren't labels flexible enough? what's the exact client behavior we want to enable?

maria: labels are messy for client-side resolution. we want an offline check: given a token/namespace, the client can say if a pin applies to this tenant/context with a simple exact match. labels are fuzzy and require control-plane semantics.

sam: i like the determinism. prefer explicit over ad-hoc label conventions. also reduces accidental collisions across teams.

kai: concrete semantics proposal: binding.namespace supports three conceptual values: "" (global), an opaque tenant-scoped id, or a logical namespace id. clients do exact equality. resolution order: tenant-id match > namespace match > global.

alex: security question - embedding clear tenant ids in public metadata could expose tenant existence. propose public endpoints return opaque namespace tokens (hashed/uuid) and private control-plane can use clear-text.

maria: agreed. for public API return "ns_2f9a..." style tokens. control-plane maps tenant -> token. that avoids enumeration.

sam: what about migration? we have thousands of existing pins encoded via labels. plan?

maria: migration sketch:
1) introduce optional binding.namespace (nullable)
2) publish mapping table to internal clients; public clients get opaque tokens
3) run 2-week graceful window: clients prefer namespace if present but continue legacy label check if absent
4) after window, require namespace check and deprecate label-based resolution

kai: edge case: tenant revokes their pin but global pin exists for same model. do we want silent fallback to global? i think not — revocation intent should be preserved.

sam: suggest tenant pins have a "state" field: active | disabled | revoked. client resolution treats disabled/revoked as explicit no-match, avoiding fallback.

alex: tie-breakers if multiple pins have same specificity? choose newest created_at, then deterministic fallback by model_ref lexical ordering. document it.

maria: quick schema draft (example only):
```
{
  "rollout_id": "str",
  "model_ref": "str",
  "binding": {
    "type": "soft|hard",
    "namespace": "nullable-string(opaque)",
    "state": "active|disabled|revoked",
    "expires_at": "rfc3339|null"
  },
  "priority": "int optional",
  "constraints": { "region": ["us-west1"], "capacity_tier":"dedicated|hosted" }
}
```

alex: telemetry request - add metric pin_match_scope{global,tenant,namespace} and pin_resolution_outcome{matched,explicitly_disabled,fellback}

ops-bot: feature-flag scheduled: "binding.namespace" api field will be enabled in control-plane on Wed 02:00 UTC. rollout via canary to 10% of tenants.

sam: we should also add a linter in sdks that flags codepaths relying solely on labels for pin logic. helps migration.

maria: final ask: docs + sample resolver algorithm in client sdk README. i'll draft a short PR for the schema and migration plan. thanks everyone!
